body.statement: Almost surely, the constrained and unconstrained GCM slopes differ only on a finite contact interval at every \(x\), the integral \(D(x)\) is finite and nonnegative, and \(D\) has a separable locally bounded stationary version. Moreover, the joint contact radius for all \(x\) in a bounded interval has a tail sufficient for independent truncation of well-separated Brownian blocks.
body.justification: The continuum maximum and any declustering rule are meaningful only after the nonlocal GCM energy is localized and given a separable version.
body.gap: Banerjee and Wellner (2001) prove the one-point LR integral is well defined; the uniform contact-radius and local-boundedness statement for the translated field is not supplied there.
body.consumer: It licenses finite-window simulation, block separation, and fine-grid approximation for the canonical calibration.

obligation.what_is_open: A locally bounded separable version and a quantitative common contact-radius tail over compact sets of constraint locations have not been constructed.
obligation.obstruction: Parabolic drift localizes individual Brownian variational pictures heuristically, but does not alone control all remote supporting chords for both one-sided constrained GCMs uniformly over a continuum. The phrase sufficient for independent truncation also lacks a numerical tail statement.
obligation.attempted: Brownian translation and affine GCM equivariance were used to prove exact finite-dimensional stationarity. Bounding the common radius solely by an argmin of Brownian motion plus a parabola leaves the remote supporting-chord events untreated.
obligation.partial_result:
The stationarity part follows exactly whenever the two GCM energies are well defined.  For \(x,t\in\mathbb R\), define \(\mathbb W_x(t)=\mathbb W(x+t)-\mathbb W(x)\).  Then
\[
 X(x+t)-X(x)-2xt=\mathbb W_x(t)+t^2.
\]
Affine equivariance of greatest convex minorants and the substitution \(s=x+t\) give
\[
 D(x)=\Phi(\mathbb W_x),
\]
where \(\Phi\) is the origin-constrained Brownian--GCM energy.  Stationary Brownian increments imply that, for every \(h\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 (\mathbb W_{x_1+h},\ldots,\mathbb W_{x_m+h})
 \stackrel{d}{=}
 (\mathbb W_{x_1},\ldots,\mathbb W_{x_m}),
\]
and hence the finite-dimensional distributions of \(D\) are translation invariant.  This identity supplies neither a common finite contact radius over a compact continuum of \(x\)'s nor the quantitative tail needed to truncate separated Brownian blocks.  It also does not by itself construct a locally bounded separable modification.
